dedupe_keys.name: 30 days of flooding effect on telecommunications and it in rio grande do sul pam 2025

description: In May 2024 weeks of severe rainfall in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil damaged infrastructure in more than 400 cities and affected 2.3 million people. This study builds telecommunications datasets for that period, combining Internet measurements, fibre cut reports and Internet Exchange routing data, and correlates network disruptions with hydrological and operational factors. The datasets offer insight into the resilience of fibre networks, data centres and Internet traffic under stress; for each scenario the authors examine failures in the information and communication technology infrastructure and the challenges they raise. Preliminary findings cover restoration of connectivity, infrastructure vulnerabilities and changes in user behaviour. Producer: Bertholdo and colleagues, presented at the Passive and Active Measurement Conference 2025 and published in Springer LNCS; the arXiv version has 32 pages and 15 figures. Coverage: one Brazilian state over about a month. Access: free preprint and a published chapter; the abstract page does not state where the datasets can be downloaded. Licence and cost: free to read, licence CC-BY-4.0 (the paper, as linked on its arXiv abstract page). Caveats: preliminary analysis of a single event, and dataset availability must be confirmed in the paper. Simulation uses: it documents the sequence of fibre, power and routing failures needed to calibrate cascading-failure and recovery models of telecom and exchange infrastructure. It relates to the legacy mobile network study of the same flood (case_study-southern-brazil-flood-2024-legacy-mobile-networks).
